To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
B cells induce RANKL-dependent osteoblast bone resorption via PGE2 production by osteoblastic cells.
cell adhesion between B cells and bone marrow osteoblasts induces the expression of RACKL in osteoblast, and that the expression is regulated by PGE produced from osteoblasts.
cell adhesion to B cells induces RANKL expression by PGE production in osteoblastic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between B cells and the production of RANKL in osteoblast, and the role of PGE in the process of RANKL expression.
the role of prostaglandins in the pathogenesis of estrogen deficiency-induced osteoporosis.
the relationship between B cells and bone metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction between B cells and bone cells induces the production of PGE in osteoblast and the production of RANKL in osteoblast by PGE.
PGE is involved in RANK-L-dependent bone resorption in OVX mice, and PGE may be a potential target for the treatment of osteoporosis.
the interaction of B cells with osteoblasts increases the production of PGE by osteoblast and the PGE production may be involved in RANK expression in osteoblastic cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
B-lymphocyte adhesion to the bone surface increases PGE production by COX-2/mPGES1 and RANKL expression by PGE/EP4 in osteoblast, and these changes may contribute to bone loss in osteoporosis.
B-lymphocyte induced bone resorption is mediated by PGE production in osteoblastic cells.
B-lymphocyte adhesion induces RANKL expression by PGE production in osteoblastic cells, and this process may contribute to bone loss in estrogen-deficient mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the increased PGE production in osteoblastic cells is induced by the cell-cell interaction with B cells in the bone marrow and the increased PGE may contribute to bone resorption through the induction of RANKL in osteoblast cells.
the cell adhesion between bone marrow B cells and osteoclasts is a critical step to initiate bone resorption in estrogen deficiency.

B cells induce PGE2 production and RANKL expression through cell-cell adhesion to osteoblasts and that the interaction between osteoblasts with B cells may be one of the mechanisms of bone resorption in osteoporosis.
